Subject: Request: waive PLG credit cap for ACME POC (exec sign-off needed)

Hi Julia —

Great catching up yesterday. ACME's engineering team is eager to move the pilot into a week-long live test against production query traffic. Our standard PLG grant covers 200k tokens / 7 days, but based on the initial load tests we ran with ACME's sample traffic (attached usage snapshot), they'll need ~800k–1M tokens to validate latency and correctness under realistic distribution.

I can extend a trial on our side, but this exceeds the standing PLG limits and requires an executive authorization to top up credits for a short POC period. Can I request sign-off to grant a one-time 1M token top-up for ACME, valid for 10 days?

Attachments: ACME_POC_scope_v2.pdf (scope), usage_snapshot_20270404.csv (sample traffic), mutual_action_plan_draft.docx

Proposed guardrails:
- One-time 1,000,000 token credit, expires 10 days from activation
- Production data may be used but logging/audit retention limited to 30 days by default
- No discounts to list pricing beyond the credit; the goal is validation only

If you OK this, I'll route to Deal Desk for final paperwork and DocuSign (MCP).

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Naomi —

Thanks for the note and attachments. Quick economics check: 1M-token top-up nets approx $1,200 in incremental cost at our blend. Given ACME's ARR potential (they've signaled ~$180k/yr if they convert) this looks reasonable as a short runway.

Two asks before I recommend exec sign-off:
- Add a simple usage guard (notify at 50% consumption and auto-disable on 120% to prevent runaway)
- Include a short commit/engagement clause in the MAP: 30-day follow-up cadence and an internal POC evaluation checklist (I sketched items in the MAP doc).

If you want, I can draft a one-line approval blurb for leadership to sign — keep it minimal: authorize one-time 1M tokens with the two guardrails above.

- Ben
